title: Q226 imaging simulation: tissue classes (CT HU, MRI T1/T2/PD at 1.5 T), structure -> class mapping rules, bone model, windows, MR sequence presets
licence: PRIVATE clinical layer (clinical/LICENSE_PRIVATE.md). Numbers are literature-based model inputs, not measurements of the two bodies.
honesty: This table drives a SIMULATION computed from segmented anatomical meshes. It is not a scan and it contains no patient data.

Every number carries a per-value status ('ver' block of each class). 'verified': the number (mean, median or range) is stated in a PubMed abstract or open full-text paragraph that was read on 2026-10-12 (citation, population and field strength in the row note and the 'ver' block). 'derived': computed from verified numbers (formula in the row). 'secondary_checked': seen only in a secondary compilation or search excerpt; the primary table was not read. 'assumption': a modelling choice with no single source. 'recalled_unverified': the Q226 value was kept but could NOT be re-read -- treat as UNVERIFIED.

MRI numbers are meant for 1.5 T. A 3 T number is used only where the row says 'derived' (T2 is nearly field independent; kidney T2, spleen T2, fat T2) and T1 values are never taken from 3 T data. Where a statistic is a range, the row states which statistic the viewer uses. Different T1 mapping methods differ by up to ~15% (ShMOLLI < MOLLI < SASHA), so T1 is method dependent. A single T1/T2 per class hides multi-exponential decay, magnetisation transfer, orientation (magic-angle) effects, B1/B0 inhomogeneity, chemical-shift and susceptibility artefacts, and motion; none of these are simulated.

Q229 verification (2026-10-12): of 165 numeric table values, 32 verified, 10 derived from verified numbers, 4 seen only in a secondary source, 76 assumptions and 43 recalled but still UNVERIFIED; 11 values changed by more than 10% against Q226 (report: data/derived/Q229_tissue_verification.json). Tables of the key papers (Gold 2004, Stanisz 2005, Bottomley 1984, de Bazelaire 1.5 T, Lamba 2014) could not be opened, so only values stated in abstracts or open full-text paragraphs count as verified.
Flow (void / inflow) and the post-gadolinium T1 values are schematic.

bone_model.note: The meshes are outer surfaces only. Cortex vs medullary / cancellous interior is MODELLED from the slice itself: pixels within a cortical thickness of the bone edge = cortical bone; inside, long-bone shaft (central part of the PCA axis) = medullary canal (yellow marrow), otherwise cancellous bone. Thicknesses are assumptions (femoral mid-shaft cortex ~ 5-7 mm of a ~28 mm outer diameter is the anchor), NOT measured on these bodies.

flat_irregular.label: vertebra / pelvis / scapula / rib / carpal / tarsal ...

bone_model.skin_note: the thin skin rim is drawn at the body boundary of the slice (assumption: dermis + epidermis ~ 1.5-2 mm on the trunk)

baseline.note: Space inside the skin that no structure covers = subcutaneous / intermuscular fat and loose connective tissue (a documented ASSUMPTION: the segmentations do not contain every fascial plane and fat pad). Outside the skin = air. Where the model has no skin (arms or feet cut by the field of view) the slice shows air there.

mapping_rules.render_note: render = 'sheet': a thin sheet-like structure (fascia, septum, capsule, retinaculum, dura ... open surfaces in the meshes) is drawn as a one-pixel line where the plane crosses it and painted after the solids; every other structure is filled (even-odd).
mapping_rules.note: First matching rule wins. Input = viewer category (cat), structure id and name (lower case, underscores -> spaces), vt ('v' = Z-Anatomy vein flag). Regexes use only the JS/Python common subset so the report script and the add-on agree (a test compares them).

rules.why: all other bones: thin cortex + cancellous interior
joint capsules, membranes, retinacula = thin fibrous SHEETS: drawn as a line where the plane crosses them, not filled
fascia, septa, aponeuroses, retinacula = thin fibrous SHEETS (open surfaces in the meshes): drawn as a line, not filled
ligaments and tendons = dense fibrous tissue (filled bands)
bursae and tendon sheaths = synovial fluid
central white-matter tracts filed under nerve
central gray structures filed under nerve (Z-Anatomy)
spinal cord (names with 'white matter' are caught next)
gyri, sulci, lobes, nuclei = gray matter
Z-Anatomy files the spleen under lymph
other solid organs, ducts, glands and pelvic organs

fallback.why: no rule matched: generic soft tissue, listed in the mapping report
